The likely fault is in [detector/wordpress.go](/app/detector/wordpress.go:37). `WpCveInfo` has no fields for `description`, `poc`, `introduced_in`, or `cvss`, so JSON decoding discards them. [extractToVulnInfos](/app/detector/wordpress.go:182) then leaves the record’s summary, severity metrics, and optional metadata unset.

The same function already carries over the `wpscan` source, URLs in input order, `vuln_type`, and `fixed_in`. It also creates a record for **every** `references.cve` value, while the requirement specifies the first. Timestamps are copied without explicit UTC normalization. [convertToVinfos](/app/detector/wordpress.go:165) processes every top-level version key, which could mix versions if a payload contains more than one.

A fix should cover enriched and null or absent fields, including an empty optional map. The repository has no Enterprise payload fixture, so the exact `cvss` JSON shape remains uncertain. Existing [WordPress tests](/app/detector/wordpress_test.go:13) cover only inactive-package filtering. I recorded the findings in [.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md); project source and tests were left unchanged.

Updated [WordPress ingestion](/app/detector/wordpress.go) to map Enterprise summaries, proof-of-concept and introduced-version metadata, and CVSS metrics. It now selects the requested core version, uses the first CVE reference, preserves URL order and UTC timestamps, and keeps records without a fix version.

Added enriched, null, and absent-field coverage in [WordPress tests](/app/detector/wordpress_test.go). `go test ./detector -count=1` and `git diff --check` passed.
